messages:
maya: heads-up — during the magnet-70b-int4 canary I saw divergent generations after a model swap + kv-cache resume on long sessions (context=65536). small prompt, then a long interact, then we swap in the int4 build and resume. output drifts after ~12k tokens.

oliver: can you paste the minimal repro and any stack/log lines?

maya: repro on my laptop: 
```
python infra/run_infer.py --model magnet-70b-int4 --context 65536 \
  --kv-cache-resume ckpt-2026-03-21-09 --stream --batch 1 \
  --prompt-file tests/long_session_seed.txt
```
I observed a token mismatch at resume: 
```
[INFO] kvcache: restored entries=65536 layers=60
[WARN] rope: layer12 scale_hint mismatch prev=1.0002 cur=0.9991
[ERROR] generation: token_mismatch at pos=12103 expected="the" got="then"
```

sam: weird. is the mismatch reproducible with fp16 model (no quant)?

maya: tried fp16 build on same seed -> no divergence, identical across swaps. only happens when resuming into int4 binary and only with >48k context.

li: @maya can you share the exact commit ids for the kernels and quantization table? kernel mismatch could cause rotary interpolation artefacts.

maya: sure — runtime: 2026-03-18a, quant table: qtbl-v3b. commit hash: 9f3a2e0.

oliver: could be a per-shard floating point jitter amplified by RoPE phase scaling at high offsets. int4 kernels use a different reduction ordering which changes rounding. we saw tiny phase error reports before but not this persistent drift.

sam: quick check — if you force the runtime to use fp32 rotary computation path even on int4 (switch flag --rotary-fp32) does it change?

maya: tried that. turning on --rotary-fp32 makes resume stable. suggests rotary math path is the culprit.

oliver: ok good signal. next steps: bisect quant table (v3b -> v3a -> v2) and run single-shard vs multi-shard resume to see if error accumulates cross-shard. also try the alternate kernel ordering we rolled out last week.

maya: bisect started: v3b -> v3a eliminated the drift on 2/3 runs, v2 stable. narrowing now. also reproduces when running on 2xA100 shards but not on a single GPU.

deploy-bot: canary deployment 2026-03-21T09:15Z — magnet-70b-int4 rolled to canary pool (id=canary-71). Watch eng-ml/canary-metrics.

li: if it's cross-shard accumulation, maybe our position offset normalization isn't being applied consistently when merging per-shard kv segments. check the merge code: `kv_merge_stride_align()` — there was a recent micro-optim change.

sam: note: the phase mismatch logged as 0.0009 per token -> over 12k tokens that compounds to ~10 radians -> token identity flips plausible.

maya: current hypothesis: quantized kernel reduction ordering + per-shard rotary normalization bug -> tiny per-token phase drift -> compounded over long context -> generation divergence after resume.

oliver: good concise hypothesis. assign triage: me (oliver) + maya + li. action items:
- reproduce with deterministic seed + single-thread shuffles off
- run bisect on quant tables and kernel commit range
- add additional assert in kv restore that checks per-layer phase baseline
- test `--rotary-fp32` as a mitigation in canary

maya: started a small test harness: `tests/kv_resume_rope_drift.py` — will run overnight with shards [1,2,4] and quant variants. posting logs to /tmp/rope_drift_run.log

li: I can add a fast guard in the merge path to normalize phase after merge (cheap clamp) for the canary. if it stabilizes, we can ship as emergency hotfix.

sam: thumbs up for the guard as short-term mitigation. long-term we want numeric-match kernels or ensure math-path parity.

maya: attaching quick sample diff of failing token stream (short):
```
seed: 42
... prompt ...
pos 12096: "and" -> pos 12097: "the" -> pos 12103: expected="the" got="then"
```

oliver: thanks. I'll set up a bisect job on CI and tag you both. if the guard works, deploy to canary and monitor token-level deltas in the console (redwood-console: per-token fidelity).

maya: will report back in the morning with overnight run summary. thanks all :pray:
